meaning: Slang for a promiscuous woman or prostitute. One of the most frequent terms in misogynistic posts.
context_note: Harmful when aimed at a woman leader.

meaning: "Bitch" (from Spanish). Also vented at lockdown rules and authorities.
context_note: Also used as a general swear word; harmful when aimed at a woman.
source: UN Women, COVID-19 & Misogyny (2020); Big Data Analysis

meaning: "Young lady." Used by men posing as "father figures" to infantilize women and dismiss their opinions. It prompted the counter-campaign #HijaAko.
context_note: Everyday word; harmful when used to talk down to a woman leader or activist.

meaning: "Banana." An everyday word turned into sexual innuendo against Senator Leila de Lima.
context_note: Everyday word (a banana variety); only harmful as innuendo about a woman leader.

meaning: "Floating" / "spaced out." Frames women politicians as unable to think clearly. Used against VP Leni Robredo.
context_note: Harmful when aimed at a woman leader.

meaning: "Stupid" / "idiot." Used against Robredo, often paired with clipped videos (cheap fakes) to suggest cognitive failure.
context_note: Low on its own; medium when paired with an edited video.

meaning: A Taglish portmanteau of "madame" and "dumb," used against Robredo.
context_note: Almost always an attack.

meaning: Women politicians cast as fronts for male relatives in political dynasties, unable to lead on their own.
context_note: Harmful when aimed at a woman leader.

meaning: "Held by the neck": controlled by male advisers.
context_note: Harmful when aimed at a woman leader.

meaning: Labels women politicians as overly emotional or weak.
context_note: Harmful when aimed at a woman leader.

meaning: "Low-flying dove," a euphemism for a prostitute.
context_note: Almost always an insult.

meaning: "Rape." Called the "top misogynistic attack word," used against Sara Duterte to trivialize sexual assault.
context_note: Treat as urgent when aimed at a person.

meaning: Lesbian slurs used to mock Sara Duterte's appearance and presentation.
context_note: Harmful when used to mock a woman leader.

meaning: "Keeps yapping" / "noisy." Dismisses women officials' criticism as gossip or nagging.
context_note: Also "maingay" (noisy), which is too common to flag on its own.

meaning: Red-tagging: labels women politicians and activists as communist rebels or terrorists, often without evidence. Online campaigns often precede surveillance or legal harassment. Targets include France Castro, Arlene Brosas and Liza Maza.
context_note: Urgent risk. Also used against men; flag when aimed at a named woman leader or activist.

meaning: "Tamarind theory." Blames women for harassment and rape; repeated in Parliament.
"The fitna of women": women as a danger to men and nations.
Roughly "being a woman is a disgrace."
A pun on "university" and "prostitute," claiming women who study are immoral.
"Illicit sex" (Arabic, used in Bangla), used to accuse women of immorality.
context_note: Also a religious term; harmful when used as an accusation against a woman.

meaning: Casts feminists as extremists.
context_note: Used in Indonesia and elsewhere.

meaning: "Men are the real victims"; claims women's reports are false.

term: एक महिला ने अपने पति को जिंदा जला दिया
meaning: "A woman burned her husband alive," reshared to argue that women are dangerous.

term: wives are more dangerous than covid
meaning: Spread in memes after a minister compared the pandemic to controlling a wife.

meaning: Labels (translated) for women who stray from being "good wives and mothers."
context_note: Translated from Indonesian and far too common to flag on its own. Needs the original Indonesian words.

meaning: Used as insults aimed at women and people of diverse genders.
context_note: Translated from Thai and too common to flag on its own. Needs the original Thai words.
